Figure 2. UMS Pipeline. The system jointly trains two 3D object detectors for multi-agent and single-agent perception. Candidate Propos-
als are first generated from two initialized weak detectors and then refined by (i) Proposal Purifying Filter (PPF), (ii) Progressive Proposal
Stabilizing (PPS), and (iii) Cross-View Consensus Learning (CCL), enabling robust pseudo supervision without human annotations.

Effect of Iterations. Table 7 reports how multi-agent detec-
tion performance changes with the number of refinement it-                         In this paper, we investigated the challenge of unsupervised
erations. Both AP@0.3 and AP@0.5 increase steadily in the                          3D object detection in the multi-agent and single-agent per-
early stages as more partially visible objects are detected,                       ception. To overcome this limitation, we introduced UMS,
while later iterations mainly help stabilize proposal consis-                      the first unsupervised framework that jointly tackles both
tency. Performance saturates around 15–20 iterations, indi-                        multi-agent and single-agent 3D perception by leveraging
cating convergence and showing that additional refinement                          cooperative LiDAR during training without any human an-
yields only marginal gains.                                                        notations. UMS integrates three key ideas: learning hierar-
Extension to Multi-Class Detection. We also conduct ad-                            chical point cloud features to suppress background-induced
ditional experiments on the V2X-Real dataset [25] for Car                          proposal errors, stabilizing multi-view proposals across re-
and Pedestrian classes. We pretrain the filter of PPF with                         finement iterations, and enforcing cross-view consensus
the Waymo open dataset [15] that includes labeled Car and                          (geometric and BEV consistency) to guide the ego detec-
Pedestrian point clouds and use CPD [22] to generate can-                          tor. Together, these components form robust collaborative
didate Car and Pedestrian proposals. As shown in Table 8,                          guidance that yields higher-quality pseudo labels and im-
UMS consistently outperforms other unsupervised methods                            proved 3D detection performance. Experiments on the pub-
for both classes.                                                                  lic V2V4Real and OPV2V demonstrate clear improvements
Robustness under Localization Errors and Latency. We                               over other existing unsupervised methods.
